records.title: Frost Armor: keeping your stacks is the survival plan
records.summary: Frost Armor reduces the damage you take. Bungie’s June update listed roughly 35% protection at five stacks in PvE, rising to 50% at seven stacks with Whisper of Rime.
records.text:
Frost Armor reduces the damage you take. Bungie’s June update listed roughly 35% protection at five stacks in PvE, rising to 50% at seven stacks with Whisper of Rime.

Why it matters
For a tank build, uptime matters as much as the highest number. Under those published values, a hit that would deal 100 damage would deal about 65 at five stacks, or 50 at seven, before any other effects. That example is arithmetic from the patch values, not a new gameplay measurement. Bungie also described stacks wearing off one at a time, giving you a chance to refresh the buff before losing all its protection.

How to use it
1. Choose a setup with a reliable way to gain Frost Armor, and watch its stack counter during a fight.
2. If your subclass offers Whisper of Rime, compare its higher stack cap with the fragment you would give up.
3. Build and refresh your stacks before exposing yourself to sustained enemy fire; retreat when the protection starts dropping.

What to watch for
These are published PvE values. They do not establish PvP protection, and adding a second defensive effect does not mean you can simply add its percentage to Frost Armor.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: No Backup Plans: use kills to keep defensive buffs going
records.summary: Bungie changed No Backup Plans so shotgun or melee final blows extend defensive buffs you already have and start health regeneration.
records.text:
Bungie changed No Backup Plans so shotgun or melee final blows extend defensive buffs you already have and start health regeneration.

Why it matters
The interesting part is maintaining a buff that normally expires. The patch names Void Overshield, Restoration, Amplified, Frost Armor and Woven Mail. That makes this a Titan build idea centred on creating protection first, then sustaining it through close-range kills. It is especially relevant if you enjoy staying in the fight rather than stopping to rebuild your defences.

How to use it
1. Choose a separate, reliable source of the defensive buff you want to maintain.
2. Activate that buff before engaging a group.
3. Use shotgun or melee final blows to test how long you can keep it active, while watching the timer and your health.

What to watch for
No Backup Plans no longer grants a fresh Void Overshield by itself under this change. Do not build the loop around receiving an overshield from nothing. Extension duration and endgame uptime still need a live check.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Smoke Jumper: check the bonus before calling it a tank build
records.summary: Bungie’s June update reduced the maximum protection from the two-piece Smoke Jumper bonus from 50% to 40% in PvE.
records.text:
Bungie’s June update reduced the maximum protection from the two-piece Smoke Jumper bonus from 50% to 40% in PvE.

Why it matters
This matters when an old build guide promises a level of protection the set no longer provides under that patch. The word “maximum” also matters: wearing two pieces does not prove that the full bonus is active throughout a fight. Your build needs to satisfy the set’s trigger and maintain it.

How to use it
1. Read the set bonus on the two armor pieces you intend to wear.
2. Check when its protection activates and when it falls away.
3. Compare that real uptime with the stats and other armor bonuses you give up.

What to watch for
The patch’s maximum is not an always-on 40% reduction. This record does not establish a PvP value or how the bonus combines with other protection.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Controlled Burst + Charge Time masterwork: check the perk is working
records.summary: Bungie’s known-issues record reports that Controlled Burst can fail on fusion rifles with a Charge Time masterwork.
records.text:
Bungie’s known-issues record reports that Controlled Burst can fail on fusion rifles with a Charge Time masterwork.

Why it matters
A roll can look excellent on paper and still fail to deliver its advertised perk. If your fusion has this combination, test whether Controlled Burst actually activates before relying on it for a boss phase. A rating based on perk names cannot detect the practical loss of a perk that is not working.

How to use it
1. Open your fusion and check both its selected trait and masterwork.
2. If it has this combination, test a full burst against a suitable target and watch for the perk activating.
3. Compare it with another copy or another fusion before committing it to your damage loadout.

What to watch for
This is an acknowledged issue in the source we reviewed, not a fresh test of your weapon. Check Bungie’s latest issue status before assuming your copy is affected or fixed.

Source & status

records.title: The same perk twice does not automatically mean double the benefit
records.summary: Bungie has acknowledged weapons dropping with duplicate perks in both trait columns. The drop can be real without proving the perk stacks twice.
records.text:
Bungie has acknowledged weapons dropping with duplicate perks in both trait columns. The drop can be real without proving the perk stacks twice.

Why it matters
This is worth investigating if you own an unusual roll, but the useful question is whether both copies actually affect the weapon. Two identical icons are not enough to promise twice the damage, ability energy or duration. Keep an unusual copy for comparison rather than judging it only from its appearance.

How to use it
1. Inspect the selected perks in both trait columns.
2. Compare the weapon’s actual buff, damage or refund with a normal copy under the same conditions.
3. Keep the unusual roll while you establish what it does; do not treat it as a confirmed exploit build.

What to watch for
Bungie acknowledged the duplicate drops. Functional double-stacking remains a separate question for each perk.

Source & status

records.title: A free Grapple is not a free Grenade Kickstart refund
records.summary: Bungie fixed Grenade Kickstart activating from free Grapples supplied by a Grapple Tangle or the Grappler modifier.
records.text:
Bungie fixed Grenade Kickstart activating from free Grapples supplied by a Grapple Tangle or the Grappler modifier.

Why it matters
This is an important limit on an “unlimited abilities” loop. A Grapple that costs no grenade energy should not be counted as spending a grenade and earning a Kickstart refund under this correction. Otherwise a build planner can promise more grenade energy than the game actually gives you.

How to use it
1. Separate your paid Grapples from free Grapples when testing the loop.
2. Watch grenade energy after each type rather than combining them into one average.
3. Choose another supported refund source if the build relies on getting energy from every free Grapple.

What to watch for
The patch establishes the free-Grapple exception. It does not establish your exact grenade recharge time or every other refund interaction.

Source & status
Bungie published this change on 2026-06-09. Forge has not retested it in the current patch.

records.title: Lament + Stronghold: a Heavy-sword survival idea to test
records.summary: The research points to Lament for a Titan sword setup because it is a Heavy sword. Bungie limited Stronghold’s infinite guard to Heavy swords.
records.text:
The research points to Lament for a Titan sword setup because it is a Heavy sword. Bungie limited Stronghold’s infinite guard to Heavy swords.

Why it matters
That distinction matters if you are copying a sword build: you cannot assume a Special-ammo sword receives the same guard behaviour. The source also records Lament’s charged light attacks being fixed to trigger sword-based Artifact perks, with later changes partly restoring its final-combo damage and self-healing. Together these are reasons to investigate the combination, not proof of an invincible loadout.

How to use it
1. Use the Heavy sword Lament with Stronghold when testing this particular guard interaction.
2. Test guarding and Lament’s attack/healing sequence separately, then combine them.
3. Add an available sword Artifact perk only after checking that Lament’s charged attacks actually trigger it in your activity.

What to watch for
Exact protection, healing uptime and current Artifact choices are not established by these patch notes. This is a build direction, not a completed “unkillable” build.

Source & status
Based on Bungie’s 24 February and 9 June 2026 changes. The combined loop has not been retested in the current patch.

How to use it
1. Use Lightning Rod to clear a comparable group of enemies.
2. Track ammo progress or subsequent ammo availability across several repeatable groups.
3. Compare that result with ordinary bow kills before deciding whether the weapon improves your loadout’s ammo economy.

records.summary: Bungie increased the Storm Grenade’s duration by half a second and its maximum tracking speed against PvE enemies by 38%, while increasing the time it takes to reach that speed by 25%.

Why it matters
The trade-off is that a higher eventual tracking speed does not mean instant acceleration. For moving enemies, what matters is how many damage ticks actually connect during the grenade’s lifetime. The extra duration and tracking changes are reasons to compare real hit consistency rather than assume a flat damage multiplier.

1. Use Storm Grenade with Touch of Thunder for this comparison.
2. Test it against a repeatably moving PvE target.
3. Count connected ticks and the complete damage sequence, keeping your other build choices fixed.

The tracking figures are stated for combatants. They do not establish faster tracking against Guardians or a PvP kill time.

records.title: Attrition Orbs: wave launchers and rockets need fewer hits
records.summary: Bungie reduced Attrition Orbs activation to four hits for wave-frame grenade launchers and three hits for rocket launchers in Update 9.7.0.
records.text:
Bungie reduced Attrition Orbs activation to four hits for wave-frame grenade launchers and three hits for rocket launchers in Update 9.7.0.

Why it matters
Attrition Orbs can help supply Orbs of Power for armor-charge and ability loops. The June patch reduced the stated hit thresholds from ten to four for wave-frame launchers and from six to three for rockets. These are hits, not guaranteed numbers of shots or kills, and the change does not automatically apply to other grenade-launcher frames.

How to use it
1. Check that your exact weapon and selected perk socket actually contain Attrition Orbs.
2. If it is a wave-frame grenade launcher, count registered hits toward the four-hit condition; if it is a rocket launcher, compare against the three-hit condition.
3. Observe Orb creation and the resulting Armor Charge or ability effects separately, rather than assuming every explosion feeds the loop.

What to watch for
Area Denial, Adaptive and Rapid-Fire grenade launchers are not wave frames. Do not apply the four-hit wave-frame rule to them without separate evidence. The patch does not give an Orb-per-second rate, a boss-DPS gain, or a guaranteed orb from one shot.

Source & status
Official Bungie Update 9.7.0, 9 June 2026. Historical activation thresholds are sourced; current weapon eligibility, enhanced differences and practical uptime have not been retested.

records.title: Desperado: a second reload trigger beyond precision kills
records.summary: Desperado can now activate after reloading following three rapid kills, as well as its existing precision-kill reload trigger.
records.text:
Desperado can now activate after reloading following three rapid kills, as well as its existing precision-kill reload trigger.

Why it matters
The June 2026 change offers a second route to the perk when a fight produces several quick final blows without a precision finish. In Crucible, the original precision-kill reload remains the more straightforward condition to test; the three-rapid-kill route is situational, not an automatic faster time to kill.

How to use it
1. Inspect a weapon that actually has Desperado in its selected perk socket; do not assume every pulse rifle can roll it.
2. Test a precision final blow followed by a reload and check the perk indicator or firing behaviour.
3. Separately test three rapid final blows followed by a reload, and compare the activation result without assuming the same window in every activity.

What to watch for
Bungie's patch does not specify the rapid-kill time window, enhanced-perk differences, firing-rate change or Guardian TTK here. The trigger requires a reload, and three rapid kills may be unrealistic in many PvP duels. Artifact bonuses must be assessed separately and are disabled in Competitive and Trials.

Source & status
Official Bungie Update 9.7.0, 9 June 2026. Both activation routes are historical official rules; no current gameplay timing or PvP TTK has been measured in this guide.

records.title: Collective Action: the PvP bonus is smaller than the PvE bonus
records.summary: Bungie lists Collective Action at 30% extra damage against combatants but only 10% against players; enhanced is 33% and 11%, respectively.
records.text:
Bungie lists Collective Action at 30% extra damage against combatants but only 10% against players; enhanced is 33% and 11%, respectively.

Why it matters
That difference matters when planning a Crucible hand-cannon two-tap or a PvE damage loop. A Firesprite or Void Breach grants eight seconds, while an Ionic Trace, Stasis Shard, or Tangle activation grants four. Repeated activations can extend the effect up to sixteen seconds. Bungie also standardized Tangle activation around destroying it, including the impact of a thrown Tangle.

How to use it
1. Use a weapon with Collective Action and create a matching elemental pickup through your subclass or another legitimate source.
2. Collect a Firesprite or Void Breach for the published eight-second duration, or an Ionic Trace or Stasis Shard for four seconds; test the timer on your HUD.
3. For Strand, destroy a Tangle by shooting it or throwing it so that it impacts; check the weapon buff before engaging.
4. In Crucible, test the 10% base or 11% enhanced player-damage bonus separately from any other boosts before claiming a two-tap.

What to watch for
The 30% and 33% PvE bonuses are not Guardian damage. These numbers do not by themselves prove a two-shot kill, which also depends on weapon archetype, precision damage, target health, falloff and any other legal modifiers. Artifact elemental orbs only apply when that Artifact mechanic is available.

Source & status
Official Bungie Update 9.7.0, 9 June 2026; reviewed 2 November. Historical published bonuses and durations, not newly measured Crucible TTK or present-season Artifact availability.

records.title: Thorn + Necrotic Grip: two corruption effects can coexist
records.summary: Bungie fixed corruption interactions so ordinary Corruption and Potent Corruption can both remain on the same enemy.
records.text:
Bungie fixed corruption interactions so ordinary Corruption and Potent Corruption can both remain on the same enemy.

Why it matters
Thorn, Touch of Malice and Necrochasm apply the shorter stacking Corruption effect. Necrotic Grip, Spirit of the Necrotic and Osteo Striga apply longer Potent Corruption, which does not stack with itself. The June fix prevents one type from incorrectly erasing or extending the other, opening a practical Warlock damage-over-time test without assuming that either effect has infinite uptime.

How to use it
1. On Warlock, equip Necrotic Grip and Thorn if both are available, then apply Thorn's corruption to a durable enemy.
2. Apply the Necrotic Grip effect through a valid melee trigger and observe whether both damage-over-time effects persist on that enemy.
3. Compare the timing with a single-effect baseline; keep the two effect types separate when recording ticks and duration.
4. If you instead use Osteo Striga, treat its Potent Corruption as the same category as Necrotic Grip rather than another independent Potent Corruption stack.

What to watch for
Two coexisting debuffs are not a verified total DPS multiplier. The patch explicitly removed unintended cross-extension and removal; it does not publish tick damage, PvP lethality, or proof that two Potent Corruption sources stack. Freezing no longer removes Weapon of Sorrow corruption according to the same patch.

Source & status
Official Bungie Update 9.7.0, 9 June 2026; reviewed 2 November. Published interaction fix; current damage ticks, duration and Guardian breakpoints remain unmeasured.

records.title: Mothkeeper's + Ex Diris: the charge gate was fixed
records.summary: Mothkeeper's Wraps builds moth grenades from kills, and Bungie's Ex Diris fix removed the need to hold moth grenade charges for their interaction.
records.text:
Mothkeeper's Wraps builds moth grenades from kills, and Bungie's Ex Diris fix removed the need to hold moth grenade charges for their interaction.

Why it matters
The June rework grants one charge unit per red-bar kill, two per orange bar, and three per miniboss, boss or opposing Guardian. Six units prepare two moth grenades while leaving your normal grenade available between overrides. Arc moths still count as Arc grenades and blind enemies; Void moths can give allies a Void Overshield. Bungie's 23 June fix separately removed a bug that made the Ex Diris interaction depend on having active moth grenade charges. This is a useful way to investigate both PvE add-clear protection and PvP setup without treating the weapon as a proven damage or TTK winner.

How to use it
1. Equip Mothkeeper's Wraps and Ex Diris on your Hunter, then use your normal grenade before the conditional override is ready.
2. Earn your own final blows and watch the moth charge progress; six red bars, three orange bars or two opposing Guardians are source-derived examples of reaching six units.
3. Test the Ex Diris interaction both before earning moth charges and after the two-grenade override appears; observe Arc blind and ally Void Overshield separately.

What to watch for
These are official historical patch rules, not current gameplay measurements. Teammate kills, assists, grenade charge overflow, exact Ex Diris proc ownership, boss DPS and Guardian TTK are not established. Artifact perks do not operate in Competitive or Trials.

Source & status
Bungie 9.7.0 published 9 June 2026; Ex Diris interaction fix published in 9.7.0.2 on 23 June 2026. Reviewed 2 November 2026, not independently gameplay-tested.

records.title: Jade Rabbit: precision kills build stacks, Firefly splash keeps them

player.takeaway: Jade Rabbit's revised Fate of All Fools gains a stack on precision kills, loses one on direct body-shot damage and no longer loses stacks merely by reloading.
player.explanation: Bungie's update raised the magazine to 15 and added Firefly. Precision kills refill the magazine; Firefly's explosion scales with Fate stacks, but splash damage does not spend them. With the catalyst, a special reload consumes stacks for a single Micro Missile round whose bonus damage depends on the stacks spent. That creates a precision-first setup to investigate in Crucible and PvE.
steps: Watch the Fate of All Fools stack counter after a precision final blow and after a reload.
Compare direct body-shot damage with Firefly splash to verify which event removes a stack.
If the catalyst is active, test the special reload at different stack counts and record the missile's actual damage against controlled targets.
player.watch_out: The 15-stack cap is a maximum, not an assumed achievable Crucible sequence. The catalyst missile damage and Guardian TTK have not been measured, and the patch does not prove the weapon is the fastest scout rifle.
